title: Civilian politics remains fragile after the Zia era
detail: Bangladesh returned formally to electoral politics after martial-law transitions, but the post-1975 order remained unstable, factional, and highly exposed to military influence.

title: Ershad seizes power
detail: Army Chief Hussain Muhammad Ershad ousted President Abdus Sattar, declared martial law, and took control of the state, ending the elected government.

title: Constitutional order is curtailed and military authority expands
detail: The new regime suspended normal constitutional processes, elevated military administrators, and reorganized the state around emergency-style executive control.

title: Military rule seeks civilian legitimacy
detail: Ershad gradually civilianized the regime through controlled political openings, new party organization, and presidential restructuring without surrendering authoritarian control.

title: Opposition alliances and street resistance consolidate
detail: The regime born in 1982 produced the alliances, student mobilization, and anti-authoritarian repertoire that later converged in the democratic uprising of 1990.
